conviction_note: Coface reports 9M-26 on Mon 2 Nov at 17:35 Paris, after the close, so the window is the 11-02 close to the 11-03 close. Coface's own consensus page (estimates as of 20 Oct) puts Q3 net income at EUR48m and the net loss ratio at 39.0%. The H1-26 run-rate was 37.4% and EUR54m a quarter, and Q3-25 showed no seasonal loss-ratio jump, so the print leans to a beat (print_vs_bar +5%). Three things hold p_up at 54 rather than 60+: the loss-ratio estimate has a 0.1ppt standard deviation, which looks like a number management steered analysts to; this name has sold two of its last four prints (Q3-25 -5.0%, FY-25 -3.8%); and the cost ratio is rising. abs_move 4.5 comes from the name's observed release-day reactions (median ~3.5%, range 0-6.5%) plus the CNP bid question on the 18:00 call. The findings sum (+1.3) is several times the scaled number (+0.36) because the fundamental read is a lean and the reaction function on this name is mixed.

findings.finding: Coface's own published Q3-26 consensus (as of 20 Oct) has a net loss ratio of 39.0% and net income of EUR48m. The H1-26 net loss ratio was 37.4% with quarterly net income of EUR53.6m and EUR54.2m. Q3-25 showed no seasonal loss-ratio deterioration (9M-25 39.6% vs H1-25 ~40.1%, so Q3-25 ~38.6%). Holding the H1 run-rate beats the bar by roughly EUR3-5m of net income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Actual release dates, close to next close: Q1-26 'meilleur que prévu' +2.1% (2026-05-12); H1-26 0.0%/+2.0% over two days (2026-07-30); FY-25 -3.8% (2026-02-19); 9M-25 -5.0% when the net loss ratio rose 4.1ppt (2025-11-03); H1-25 -3.3%; Q1-25 -6.5%. The loss ratio is the line this stock trades on, and good numbers are not reliably rewarded.
findings.original_quote: H1 release (fr): 'Ratio de sinistralité net à 37,4 %, en amélioration de 2,7 ppts ; le ratio combiné net stable à 71,3 %' — net loss ratio 37.4%, improved 2.7ppt; net combined ratio stable at 71.3% (https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/MKW/2026/07/FCMKW135265_20260730.pdf)
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is public, so the bar is known; the claim is that the bar sits about 1.6ppt of loss ratio above the run-rate. If the market expected a beat, the stock would not be at EUR15.54: that is below its pre-rumour level of ~EUR16.0 and well below the EUR17.7-18.0 average target, with a flat run-up. Caveats that cut it to +1.0: the 0.1ppt sd on the loss ratio suggests management signposted a normalisation, and the cost ratio (consensus 35.4%, Q3-25 ~34.5%, H1 +2.7ppt yoy) could absorb part of the beat.
findings.independence: Altares French insolvencies in Q3-26 flat (+0.5% yoy) after +5.4% in Q2 (https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-10-19-defaillances-dentreprises-au-3e-trimestre-2026-une-quasi-stabilite-selon-altares.html), filed separately as a small proxy.

findings.finding: Bloomberg reported on 18 Sep 2026 that CNP Assurances (La Banque Postale) is working on a possible offer for Coface, which would need Arch Capital's 29.9% stake. Nobody denied it. The stock has since given back the whole +8.9% and trades below its pre-rumour level, and the 9M call (18:00 CET, inside the window) is the first time management takes questions since.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one observation: +8.9% on 2026-09-18 on 0.5% of the capital traded, then a full round-trip to EUR15.4-15.5 by late October with no follow-up story found.
findings.original_quote: Boursier.com via Fortuneo, 18/09/2026 17:48: 'Selon l'agence Bloomberg, CNP, détenu par la Banque Postale, travaillerait sur une offre potentielle pour l'acquisition du leader de l'assurance-crédit' — according to Bloomberg, CNP, owned by La Banque Postale, is working on a potential offer to acquire the credit-insurance leader (https://bourse.fortuneo.fr/actualites/coface-flambe-avec-la-rumeur-cnp-2848710)
findings.why_not_priced: The full round-trip to below the pre-rumour price means the market now prices close to zero bid probability. A denial therefore costs little, while any confirmation or 'approach received' comment on the call would reprice the stock toward the ~EUR3bn (~EUR20/share) valuation analysts floated. The expected value is small because the most likely answer on the call is 'no comment'. The company is not in an offer period, so the 'in a live bid results are noise' rule does not apply.
findings.independence: AMF threshold declarations in June 2026 show CNP Assurances crossing 5% via shares received as collateral (4.62% held, 6.00% total CDC group on 11 June, back to 1.38% on 18 June): https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/307/8888/01/FC307636385_20260706.pdf. That is a securities-lending artefact and not evidence of intent.

findings.finding: Arch Capital, Coface's 29.9% holder, reported on 27-28 Oct that Q3-26 catastrophe losses rose to $234m, including undisclosed Iran-war claims in war-risk lines. Coface's H1 release named the closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a shock, so its single-risk/political-risk book could carry Q3 claims that the consensus does not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed Coface reaction to a political-risk claim surprise in the sampled history.
findings.original_quote: H1 release (fr): 'une croissance économique qui reste faible et soumise à des chocs répétés (droits de douane, fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz)' — economic growth that remains weak and subject to repeated shocks (tariffs, closure of the Strait of Hormuz)
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company transmission hypothesis: neither Coface nor a direct counterparty has said Coface took Iran-related claims, and Arch's losses sit in marine and land war lines Coface barely writes. If it were priced, the consensus loss ratio would sit above Q3-25's, and at 39.0% it partly does. Sized as a small proxy.

findings.finding: Altares counted 14,652 French business failures in Q3-26, +0.5% year on year, after +5.4% in Q2-26. France is a minority of Coface's claims, but the series points to a benign quarter in a core market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable in Coface's history; the 9M-25 loss-ratio rise came alongside record insolvencies and the stock fell 5%.
findings.original_quote: 'une tendance quasiment stable par rapport à l'an passé' — a trend almost stable compared with last year (Altares Q3-2026 study, as reported; also https://tpeactu.fr/2026/10/13/defaillances-entreprises-t3-2026-altares-tpe/)
findings.why_not_priced: It is a national proxy on a global book: Coface's H1 release said corporate failures remain at record levels worldwide. The market has the series, but nothing shows it moving the Q3 loss-ratio estimate, which sits above the run-rate. Small because the transmission is partial.
findings.independence: Coface's own H1 loss-ratio run-rate (finding 1) points the same way; a different source.

outside_window.finding: Coface promised at H1 to make up the dropped 50bp 2027 RoATE contribution from information services with an additional dividend ('Coface compensera ce manque à gagner par un dividende additionnel'). The company-compiled consensus carries an additional distribution per share of EUR0.00 for 2026-2028, and solvency is 194%, above the 155-175% range. This resolves with the FY-26 results and dividend proposal in Feb 2027.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is flat (+0.05, run-up -1.1% over 20d). The fundamental read leans mildly positive and the M&A optionality is positively skewed, so neither agrees with nor fights a lean that barely exists. The reaction history (two of the last four prints sold) is what keeps p_up near 50.

lessons_applied: 'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error' / 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5, above the name's observed ~3.5% median and toward France's 4.19% median
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' (this name sold 9M-25 and FY-25): the loss-ratio finding cut from +1.2 to +1.0 and p_up moved from 56 to 54
'In a live bid, results are noise': checked and not applicable, because Coface is not in an offer period (rumour only), so the CNP finding stays small
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the Arch/Iran and Altares proxies were already small; left unchanged rather than applied twice
